note: Set B's five claims all match the page text exactly (KP(θ=0º)=0.01882681 s, KI(θ=0º)=0.008068634, KD=0.0 s², ζφ=0.7 with its stated rationale). Set A repeats those same five correct claims but adds six chart-derived claims, five of which are wrong: three bind right/left axis tick labels (0.000, 0.020, 0.0) as if they were the gain or gain-correction factor at 0º, directly contradicting the correct KP/KI values and the fact that GK(0º)=1.0, and one reads the proportional gain at 20º as 0.010 s when the blue curve is near 0.005 s. Only A's gain-correction factor ≈0.2 at 20º is a defensible chart read. B is therefore clearly the better set.
remarks: A's three '0.000/0.020/0.0 at 0º' claims are axis-tick artifacts of the figure's dual y-axes, not data points; the extractor paired tick labels with the x-axis origin. Both sets state ζφ = 0.7 twice (once as the upper limit of the recommended range, once with the generator-torque negative-damping rationale) - arguably one fact with two conditions. Both sets also omit the gain-scheduling law GK(θ) = 1/(1 + θ/θK) and the implementation detail that the previous time step's blade-pitch angle is used to compute the next time step's gain-correction factor. Chart-read values in A carry fabricated-looking concatenated quotes ('... 0.000 ... 0') that do not correspond to any real text span.
